newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle bid $65.00, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle bid $65.00, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids near midday on Monday were light at $65.00 per cwt and passed by owners pricing cattle $67.00-$68.00, feedlot sources said.
"Packers are telling us they have plenty of cattle and are not in any hurry to buy for awhile," a Kansas feedlot manager said.

Sales were seen taking place Wednesday or Thursday. Active sales last week and increased availability of contract and formulated cattle when calendar pages flipped to a new month on Friday kept buying interest light, several sources said.
Cattle owners anticipated fed cattle prices to be underpinned by outlooks for smaller showlists this week and recent firm beef prices, cattle feeders said.
However, early estimates pegged showlists steady to slightly smaller than a week ago and beef prices appeared to be near a top after last week's climb, they said.
USDA quoted boxed beef values down $0.18 per ctw to up $0.19. Heavier-weight choice was quoted down $0.01 at $108.86 after jumping $4.10 per cwt higher last week.
"There's a little concern that the meat business could be slowing because of the higher money," a market source said.
